summary: Xiuzhi Zeng works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her MA at Nanhua University under Meihua Chen, attested in 2006.

Xu Dishan (1893–1941) was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Yenching, Columbia, and Oxford, and held posts at Peking University (~1926–1930), Tsinghua University (~1930–1935), and the University of Hong Kong (~1935–1941).

Xue Yu (b. 1964) specializes in Buddhist and religious studies and earned an MPhil from the University of Hong Kong. He held posts at CUHK, the University of Chicago (attested 2026), and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Xuesong Zhang works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xue Yu (attested 2008) and held an associate professor position at Renmin University of China (attested 2015).

Xuezhu Li specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, and studied under Shoryu Katsura. He served as a Numata fellow at Ryukoku University (2011) and as a research associate at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2010–2026).
Y. B. Damle studied under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. He held a post as Professor of Sociology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).
Yadi Qu works in Indology, Tibetology, and computational studies. As of 2026, she studied and held a position as Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin at the University of Hamburg.

Yael Bentor specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University Bloomington, where she completed her doctorate under Gregory Schopen in 1991, and has held professorial posts at Hebrew University.

Yakupitiyage Karunadasa (1934–2026) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD under David Friedman at the University of London. He was Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and held visiting posts at SOAS, Calgary, Toronto, and HKU.
Yandong Hou is a scholar in Tibetology. He studied at and held a post at the Nanjing Institute of Geography and Limnology.

Yanfei Zhao specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Zhao earned an MA at Beijing Foreign Studies University (2016–2019) and an MA at SOAS (2021–2022), continuing doctoral work at BFSU and Yale University.
Yanfei Zhou specializes in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and sinology. Zhou earned a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet-Keung Lo.
Yang-Gyu An is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford in 1998 under Richard Gombrich, having also studied under Hojin.
Yangdon Dhondup (b. 1970) is a Tibetology scholar. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Henry Y. H. Zhao (~2000–2004).
Yanling Chen is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University (attested 2012) under Yongdong Shi, having also studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

Yannick Laurent works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. Attested in 2026, he has held posts at the University of Munich and as Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Yanpei (1917–1996) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Taixu (~1934–1939) and Yinshun (~1941–1945).
Yao Wang (1928–2015) was a scholar in Tibetology and sinology who studied under Gongkar Tulku and served as a guest professor at the University of Vienna.
Yao-ming Tsai specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of California by 1997 and served as Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.
Yaping Dou specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Xue Yu (attested 2010).
